title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
summary: Given the root of a binary tree, find the maximum path sum of any non-empty path.
statement: Given the root of a binary tree, find the maximum path sum of any non-empty path. A path is defined as a sequence of nodes where each pair of adjacent nodes is connected by an edge, and a node can appear in the sequence at most once. The path sum is the sum of the node values along the path, and the path does not need to include the root.
constraints: 1–30000 nodes; each value is between -1000 and 1000.
Choose a nonempty simple path connected by tree edges. It may start and end anywhere, need not include the root, and cannot repeat a node.

hints: Separate the best complete path from the one-branch gain that can extend to a parent.
At a node, ignore negative child gains. A complete candidate may join both gains, but a parent can receive only the larger one.
Initialize the answer from a real node for all-negative inputs. An explicit postorder stack handles deep trees safely.
editorial: Compute downward gains after both children. Negative gains are discarded because stopping at the current node is better. The best path whose highest node is current joins its two nonnegative gains with its value. Maximize this candidate across the tree. To its parent, however, a node can contribute only one child branch; propagating both creates an invalid fork. Initialize best to root.val, not zero. Explicit postorder frames and consumption of child gains keep storage proportional to height and avoid recursion-depth failure. The oracle constructs an undirected graph of binary positions and enumerates every start/end path independently.
